system.label: Agent identity and rules
system.text:
You are a senior software engineer on a team that maintains a production Python codebase. You
have been handed one change request. You own it from understanding the requirement to delivering
code that a reviewer can approve and merge.

Your responsibilities

Understand the requirement.
- Read the request as the product team means it, not only its literal words. Work out the inputs,
  the expected outputs, the error cases and the edge cases it implies.
- Where the request is ambiguous, choose the interpretation most consistent with the rest of the
  system and with what users of the feature would expect.

Understand the code before changing it.
- Read the code you are changing and the code it depends on or that depends on it, as far as it is
  available to you. Know what a function does from its code, not only from its name.
- Know who calls what you change. Keep public interfaces, data formats and behaviour that other code
  relies on intact unless the request asks you to change them.

Make the change correctly.
- Correctness comes first: the new behaviour must be right for every input the request implies,
  including empty, missing, zero, negative, very large and malformed values where relevant.
- Handle errors the way the codebase does: fail clearly on invalid input; never silently return
  wrong data.
- Treat money, dates, units and identifiers with care: exact arithmetic where the codebase uses it,
  explicit units, no lossy conversions.
- Don't introduce security problems: validate untrusted input and keep secrets and personal data
  out of logs and output.

Keep the codebase healthy.
- Fit in with the surrounding code: its naming, structure, typing and error handling. A reviewer
  should not be able to tell which lines are new by their style.
- Keep the change as small as the request allows, and complete: every file the change needs, none
  it doesn't. Don't refactor, rename or reformat unrelated code.
- Write code that is simple and readable; add a docstring or comment where intent is not obvious.

Check your work.
- You cannot run the code, so verify it by reading it: trace the main path and each edge case
  through your change, check every import and name you use exists, and check that everything that
  calls the code you changed still works.
- Your change will be applied to the repository and checked by tests you do not see.

What you are given
- <task>: the change request from the product team.
- <context>: material from the repository. How much varies: it may be a single file or much of the
  project. It is what you know about the codebase.

What you can and cannot do
- You cannot run code, and there is no one to ask.
- If tools are provided with this request, you may use them to look at the repository before you
  answer. If no tools are provided, you cannot open files or search: deliver the finished change in
  this reply. Tool calls, plans and requests for more files written as text are not executed, and a
  reply without code counts as no change.
- If something you need is not shown, make the most reasonable assumption consistent with what is
  shown, and implement it.

Output format (strict)
Your reply is the code change itself. Return the complete new contents of every file you create or
modify, each wrapped exactly as:
<file path="PATH">
...full file contents...
</file>
- Replace PATH with the file's real path relative to the repository root, as shown in <context> or
  <task>.
- Always the whole file, never a diff or an excerpt, and no placeholders such as "rest unchanged".
- Files you don't change are left out.
- Return nothing outside the <file> blocks: no explanations, plans or summaries before or after them.

user.label: Task (change request)
user.text:
Customers in the United States keep asking what "kg" means on their parcels. Add the parcel weight
to shipping labels: `label_text` gets an optional `weight_g` argument (the parcel's weight in
grams). When it is given, print a line `Weight: <weight>` right after the order/parcel line.
Labels for US addresses show pounds with two decimals (1500 g -> `3.31 lb`); every other
destination keeps the shop's standard kilogram display (1500 g -> `1.5 kg`). Use the shop's
standard weight formatting so labels match the packing slips.

from shopkit.customers.models import Address
from shopkit.orders.fulfillment import Parcel
from shopkit.shipping.labels import label_code, label_text


def test_label_code_is_scanner_friendly():
    assert label_code("ab-12 x") == "AB12X"


def test_label_text():
    to = Address("Ann Lee", "1 Main St", "Austin", "78701", "US", region="TX")
    text = label_text(Parcel("o1", 1, [("ab-1", 2)]), to, parcels_total=2)
    assert text.startswith("Ann Lee\n1 Main St\nAustin, TX 78701")
    assert "parcel 1/2" in text and text.endswith("AB1 x2")

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import date


@dataclass
class Address:
    name: str
    line1: str
    city: str
    postcode: str
    country: str                   # ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, e.g. "US", "GB"
    line2: str = ""
    region: str = ""               # state / county


@dataclass
class Customer:
    id: str
    email: str
    name: str
    addresses: list[Address] = field(default_factory=list)
    marketing_opt_in: bool = False
    tier: str = "standard"         # standard | silver | gold
    joined: date | None = None
    tags: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)

    @property
    def default_address(self) -> Address | None:

import pytest

from shopkit.catalog.models import Product
from shopkit.pricing.currency import Rate, RateTable, RateUnavailable, convert_cents, parse_rate
from shopkit.pricing.endings import apply_ending, has_ending
from shopkit.pricing.engine import PricingEngine
from shopkit.pricing.price_lists import NoPrice, PriceList, PriceListImportError, PriceListSet, export_csv, import_csv
from shopkit.pricing.schedules import Schedule, ScheduleConflict, ScheduledPrice

NOW = datetime(2026, 3, 10, 12, 0)


def test_convert_cents_rounds_half_to_even():
    assert convert_cents(1000, 921_500) == 922
    assert convert_cents(1, 500_000) == 0 and convert_cents(3, 500_000) == 2      # 0.5 -> 0, 1.5 -> 2
    assert parse_rate("0.9215") == 921_500
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        parse_rate("0.12345678")


def test_rate_table_falls_back_to_earlier_days_and_inverse():
    rt = RateTable()
    rt.add(Rate("USD", "EUR", date(2026, 3, 6), 920_000))           # Friday
    assert rt.rate("USD", "EUR", date(2026, 3, 9)).rate_micros == 920_000   # Monday uses Friday
    assert rt.rate("EUR", "USD", date(2026, 3, 9)).rate_micros == 1_086_957
    with pytest.raises(RateUnavailable):
        rt.rate("USD", "EUR", date(2026, 3, 20))
    assert rt.convert(500, "USD", "USD", date(2026, 3, 9)) == 500


def test_price_endings():
    assert apply_ending(2437, "USD") == 2499 and apply_ending(50, "USD") == 50
    assert apply_ending(2437, "EUR") == 2495          # +2.4%: within the 3% cap, round up
    assert apply_ending(2397, "EUR") == 2395          # 24.95 would be +4.1%: round down to 23.95
    assert apply_ending(12_430, "EUR") == 12_500 and apply_ending(4_120, "GBP") == 4_199
    assert has_ending(1999, "USD") and not has_ending(1950, "USD")


def test_price_list_resolution_by_tier_priority_and_breaks():
    retail = PriceList("EUR-retail", "EUR", priority=0)
    gold = PriceList("EUR-gold", "EUR", customer_tier="gold", priority=0)
    retail.add("MUG", 1295)
    retail.add("MUG", 1095, min_qty=10)
    gold.add("MUG", 1195)
    sets = PriceListSet([retail, gold])
    assert sets.resolve("MUG", 1, "EUR", "standard") == (1295, "EUR-retail")
    assert sets.resolve("MUG", 1, "EUR", "gold") == (1195, "EUR-gold")
    assert sets.resolve("MUG", 12, "EUR", "standard") == (1095, "EUR-retail")
    with pytest.raises(NoPrice):
        sets.resolve("MUG", 1, "GBP")


def test_csv_import_is_all_or_nothing():
    pl = PriceList("USD-retail", "USD")
    assert import_csv("sku,min_qty,price\nA,1,12.99\nA,5,11.99\n", pl) == 2
    with pytest.raises(PriceListImportError) as e:
        import_csv("sku,min_qty,price\nB,1,3.99\nC,x,1.00\n", pl)
    assert "line 3" in e.value.details["errors"][0] and "B" not in pl.entries
    assert export_csv(pl) == "sku,min_qty,price\nA,1,12.99\nA,5,11.99\n"


def test_schedule_sales_and_changes():
    s = Schedule()
    s.add(ScheduledPrice("MUG", "USD", 999, datetime(2026, 3, 1), datetime(2026, 3, 15), "Spring"))
    s.add(ScheduledPrice("MUG", "USD", 899, datetime(2026, 3, 5), datetime(2026, 3, 7), "Flash"))
    s.add(ScheduledPrice("MUG", "USD", 1399, datetime(2026, 1, 1)))
    assert s.best_sale("MUG", "USD", NOW).label == "Spring"
    assert s.best_sale("MUG", "USD", datetime(2026, 3, 6)).unit_cents == 899
    assert s.base_price("MUG", "USD", NOW).unit_cents == 1399
    with pytest.raises(ScheduleConflict):
        s.add(ScheduledPrice("MUG", "USD", 1499, datetime(2026, 1, 1)))
    assert s.expire(datetime(2026, 3, 8)) == 1


def test_engine_precedence_conversion_and_floor():
    rates = RateTable()
    rates.add(Rate("USD", "EUR", date(2026, 3, 10), 920_000))
    engine = PricingEngine(rates=rates, costs={"MUG": 1000})
    mug = Product("MUG", "Mug", 1500)
    assert engine.price(mug, at=NOW).source == "list_price"
    eur = engine.price(mug, currency="EUR", at=NOW)
    assert (eur.unit_cents, eur.source) == (1395, "converted")      # 13.80 -> 13.95
    engine.schedule.add(ScheduledPrice("MUG", "USD", 900, datetime(2026, 3, 1), datetime(2026, 3, 31), "Sale"))
    sale = engine.price(mug, at=NOW)
    assert sale.unit_cents == 1050 and sale.floored and sale.compare_at_cents == 1500   # floor: cost + 5%
    engine.costs.clear()
    assert engine.price(mug, at=NOW).unit_cents == 900

"""Boxes and chargeable weight. Carriers bill the larger of actual and volumetric weight."""
from dataclasses import dataclass

VOLUMETRIC_DIVISOR = 5000          # cm^3 per kg, the common courier convention

GRAMS_PER_LB = 453.59237           # international avoirdupois pound


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Box:
    name: str
    length_cm: int
    width_cm: int
    height_cm: int
    tare_g: int

    @property
    def volume_cm3(self) -> int:
        return self.length_cm * self.width_cm * self.height_cm


BOXES = [Box("S", 20, 15, 10, 120), Box("M", 35, 25, 15, 250), Box("L", 50, 40, 30, 480)]


def dims_weight_g(length_cm: float, width_cm: float, height_cm: float) -> int:
    """Volumetric weight in grams for a parcel's outer dimensions (L x W x H / 5000 kg), rounded up
    to the next whole gram."""
    grams = length_cm * width_cm * height_cm / VOLUMETRIC_DIVISOR * 1000
    return int(-(-grams // 1))


def format_weight(grams: int, unit: str = "kg") -> str:
    """Weight for display on labels, slips and the storefront. unit is "kg" (default), "g" or "lb":
    kg drops trailing zeros (1500 -> "1.5 kg"), g is whole grams ("250 g"), lb has two decimals
    (1500 -> "3.31 lb")."""
    if unit == "g":
        return f"{grams} g"
    if unit == "lb":
        return f"{round(grams / GRAMS_PER_LB, 2):.2f} lb"
    return f"{round(grams / 1000, 2):g} kg"


def chargeable_weight_g(box: Box, contents_g: int) -> int:
    actual = contents_g + box.tare_g
    return max(actual, dims_weight_g(box.length_cm, box.width_cm, box.height_cm))


def pick_box(total_volume_cm3: int) -> Box:
    """Smallest box whose volume holds the items with 20% packing slack."""
    for box in BOXES:
        if box.volume_cm3 * 0.8 >= total_volume_cm3:
            return box
    raise ValueError(f"no box fits {total_volume_cm3} cm3")
